main_text.p: in Targ. Hierosolymitano. Sic quoq; legendū Genef.25.14. in Jon. pro צְמִיתָא: respondet enim Hebraeo מִשְׁמַע, quod ibi est nomen proprium. Posset quoque transpositis litteris legi מִצִיתָא.
מִצָתוּת Ch. Idem, Genef.2.7. in T. Jon.
אַצָתָא Ch. Idem, Jesa.21.7. Hebr. קָשַׁב. Vel est Infinitivus Aphel.
צָחָא צָחַר Chald. Sitivit, Sitiens, sitibundus fuit.

Idem quod צְהָא: Item Elanguere, deficere, deliquium pati, siti scil. vel fame, Threm.2.11.12.19. Ex Aphel אַצְחִיאו Sitiunt, Jobi 24.11. אַצְחָנוּן Sitire fecit eos, Jesa.48.21. Deinde in Pahel Syr. ܨܚܝ Conviciari, maledicere, Turpiter & obscoenè loqui, Luxuriare. Ex Ethpah. Partic. ܡܨܚܝܢ Qui convicia passus est, 1.Pet.2.23.
צָחֵי, צָחְיָא Ch. Sitiens, sitibundus: Aridus, siccus. Foemin. בְּאֶתֶר צִיחְתָא In loco arido, Psal.23.2.
צְחוּתָא צְחוּתָא Ch. Sitis, Psal.107.33. Ruth.1.1.
צְחוּנָא Ch. Idem. בֵּית צְחוּנָא Locus sitriculosus, siccus, Deuter.8.15. in Onkelo. In Jonathane male est ב pro ח, Jesa.44.3.
ܠܐܘܠܐ Syr. Maledicentia, convitium, 1.ad Tim.5.14. 1.Pet.3.9. λοιδορία: Obscoenitas. Plural. ܠܐܘܠܐ Obscoenitates, ad Eph.5.4. Graece αἰσχρότης.
צחח צְחִיחַ Ch. Ariditas, Locus aridus, ut Hebr. Plur. צְחִיחִין, Psalm.68.6.

page.notes: Hebrew, Syriac and Greek words are transcribed as best read; several Syriac forms and vocalisation marks are uncertain and may be imperfect. Catchword and signature absent.
